acceptance_criteria.criterion: Do not weaken candidate admission or trusted-proof requirements.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: No requirement is removed. The only new outcome is pending, which is returned in place of a failure and never in place of a success. Every prior failure branch -- terminated run, foreign head, wrong workflow name or path, wrong event, unbound run, untrusted publisher, malformed status, absent run -- is preserved and independently regressed in tests/test_issue_417_governance_waiting_state.py.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Do not treat absence of proof as success.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: read_trusted_upgrade_status returns success only on the unchanged completed-and-verified path. A genuinely absent run still returns missing, which every call site maps to failure; test_no_eligible_trusted_run_at_all_stays_missing and test_a_completed_eligible_run_without_a_status_is_not_waiting pin both halves.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Distinguish at least these states deterministically: eligible trusted run in progress -> waiting/pending; eligible trusted run completed successfully and exact-head proof valid -> success; eligible trusted run completed with failure -> failure; proof malformed/stale/foreign-head/mismatched -> failure; no eligible trusted run/proof path exists where one is required -> failure.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: All five are asserted directly. Waiting is decided from run status in TRUSTED_RUN_ACTIVE_STATES for a run that passes the same identity predicate the completed proof must pass, so the decision is a function of observable run state rather than of message text.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Avoid periodic re-publication of identical red failure messages while the same trusted run is merely in progress.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: While the same head and same active run persist, the controller publishes pending with a stable description instead of a red failure, so repeated governance runs no longer emit a new red signal for an unchanged, non-defective condition.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Status text should name the dependency clearly, e.g. Waiting for trusted exact-head preflight proof.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: TRUSTED_PROOF_WAITING_DESCRIPTION is exactly that string and is pinned by test_the_waiting_description_names_the_dependency. It is a constant consumed by the decision, never parsed by it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add deterministic tests covering the state transitions above, including the PR #416 scenario where governance was red only because the trusted run had not finished yet.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/test_issue_417_governance_waiting_state.py adds 31 fixtures including test_the_same_head_succeeds_once_the_trusted_proof_lands, which drives the PR #416 sequence on byte-identical candidate content: waiting while the run is active, then success once the proof exists. Thirteen of the new fixtures were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix source and pass against the repair.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No auto-Ready, auto-merge, force-push, or weakening of human merge approval.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: No readiness, promotion or merge authority is added. The merge-readiness change is strictly restrictive: a governance pending that previously passed now blocks. The candidate-admission controller leaves a waiting head untouched rather than promoting it. The push was fast-forward through the real pre-push boundary.

defect_families.evidence: No authorization is minted, consumed or re-aimed. The change reads run state and returns a verdict; the trusted proof's own authorization semantics are untouched, and the identity predicate that binds a run to one exact head and one pull request is now shared rather than duplicated, so it cannot drift on one path only.

Nothing new is written or trusted from candidate-supplied content. Run status, name, path, event, head_sha and pull_requests all come from the Actions API read by the trusted default-branch controller; a candidate cannot forge them, and no decision reads message text.

No channel's proof obligation changed. Both the connector-origin and ordinary-candidate branches still require the trusted hosted exact-head proof; only the reported state while that proof is legitimately in flight changed, from failure to pending.

Both commits in this range carry author and committer Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>, the identity bound to login 'claude' in writer_identity_binding, with agent attribution confined to trailers. The push boundary validated the governed range before any remote mutation.
Two substantive commits, published by ordinary fast-forward pushes. No commit is empty, no rewind or force-push was performed, and no intermediate commit is stranded.

This candidate writes no connector authorization receipt, so the inherited-receipt path applies and makes no claim about this range. _validate_receipt_freshness is unmodified and ran at the push boundary.

verify_pre_ready_hostile_review is unmodified and still gates admission ahead of the trusted-proof dependency. This review is the artifact it requires, recorded against the exact base->HEAD content; test_a_real_blocker_alongside_an_active_run_is_failure_not_waiting proves a stale review still outranks an active trusted run.

This family recurred and is the subject of the change. The tri-state existed and propagated correctly, but the evidence source did not: the trusted workflow publishes its status from its final job, so an absent status was read as an absent proof path for the entire time the proof was being produced. The family's invariant and prevention mechanism now state that 'still running' is decided from observable run state for the exact head rather than from the presence of a published status, and five new regressions are declared. Adversarially probed: unavailable and malformed run evidence fail closed rather than reporting a wait, an ineligible lookalike run earns no wait on any of the four identity fields, an unbound run earns none, and a concurrent independent blocker outranks the wait.

No lifecycle stage is raised. DFF-014 remains hosted-enforced with a resolvable non-test guard reference at a machine boundary; only its invariant, mechanism, regression evidence and sources were strengthened to describe what the code now actually enforces.

Validation-proof identity and reuse are untouched by this change. No file under the reuse authority is modified, no proof identity rule is altered, and the #416 validation-performance behaviour is unchanged.

findings.evidence: Merge readiness passed a pending governance status through whenever mergeability was resolved, on the premise that governance could publish pending only while mergeability was unresolved. Issue #417 invalidates that premise: governance now publishes pending to mean the required trusted exact-head proof is still running, which readiness cannot derive for itself, so the shortcut would have let a candidate reach ready-to-merge on a proof that does not yet exist. Repaired by making governance pending block as pending. It cannot become a permanent lock because the governance controller republishes on every event and on its schedule. The test that encoded the old premise was replaced with one that states the new contract and the reason for it, and a paired fixture proves a successful governance status still passes.

Adding the active-run lookup introduced a second GitHub read on the no-status path, which surfaced a pre-existing test fake in tests/test_pr376_prevention_regressions.py that answered every request path with the same status list. The PR #376 invariant is unchanged; its fake now answers each read separately so it keeps testing wrong-PR authorization rather than incidentally exercising the new lookup.

The waiting lookup issues one additional Actions API request, and only on the branch where no matching status exists. A completed candidate takes the unchanged path and costs nothing extra; the added cost falls exactly on the window the change exists to describe correctly.

The hosted full lane refused head ab6aa64: tests/test_hunter_workflow_state.py::test_all_checks_green_inherits_the_canonical_stale_governance_allowance asserted that a governance status of pending on a mergeable head is green, which is the canonical allowance this Issue removes. scripts/hunter_workflow_state.py derives ALL_CHECKS_GREEN by evaluating a blocker-neutralised observation through the canonical merge-readiness decision precisely so it keeps no copy of that policy, so the evaluator itself needed no change and correctly inherited the new block; only its test expectation and a docstring naming the old allowance were stale. Repaired by stating the inherited behaviour, with a paired fixture proving a successful governance status still reaches MERGE_READY so the block is state-specific rather than a blanket refusal. The full suite passes on the repaired content (3,747 passed).
